patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient’s mother reports that the infant occasionally stops breathing while sleeping, with episodes increasing in frequency. The patient was born prematurely at 32 weeks due to placental insufficiency and required respiratory support immediately post-birth. Prenatal testing indicated the mother was not immune to rubella. The pregnancy was otherwise uncomplicated, with the mother taking only prenatal vitamins. The family history includes a healthy 3-year-old sister and a father with a heart condition.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Episodes of not breathing (apnea) during sleep

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Premature birth at 32 weeks due to placental insufficiency. Stay in the neonatal intensive care unit for respiratory support.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: The patient’s mother took prenatal vitamins. Father has a heart condition. One healthy sibling.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Patient has pale conjunctiva but no other symptoms or complaints provided by the mother.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the infant presenting with episodes of apnea and anemia.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: My mother says I sometimes stop breathing while sleeping, and the episodes are becoming more frequent. He was born at 32 weeks and needed respiratory support right after birth. We also noticed his conjunctiva looks pale.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any areas of your skin that are scratched, rubbed raw, or have small open spots (excoriations)?
turns.patient_answer: Doctor, I haven’t had any scratched or rubbed raw skin, and I’m not aware of any small open spots or excoriations.

turns.doctor_question: After your minor injury, have you noticed any signs that a bone might be broken—like severe pain, swelling, bruising, deformity, or trouble using the area normally? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No—there was no severe pain, swelling, bruising, deformity, or any trouble using his body normally.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any redness or warmth on your **left wrist** (the skin looking red compared with the other side)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any redness or warmth on his left wrist—his skin looks the same as the other side.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bruising on your chest wall (for example, dark or discolored areas on the skin over your ribs or breastbone), especially after an injury or from coughing/strain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any bruising on his chest wall—no dark or discolored areas over his ribs or breastbone.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been urinating much more than usual lately—like needing to go to the bathroom more often or producing a larger amount of urine?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: “I’m not able to tell about how often I urinate, but my mother hasn’t mentioned any clear increase in urine amount or needing diaper changes more often than usual.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you used any substances that could affect your health—such as alcohol, tobacco/nicotine, cannabis, opioids, stimulants, or other drugs—either recently or in the past?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t used any substances like tobacco, cannabis, opioids, or stimulants—my mother hasn’t reported anything like that either.” “I’m only 1-month old, but she says the main issue is the pauses in breathing during sleep that seem to be happening more often.” “I’m not aware of anything else new.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any trouble controlling your urine—such as leaking or not making it to the bathroom in time? (yes/no)
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any trouble controlling my urine—my mother hasn’t noticed leaking or fewer wet diapers than usual.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any new or changing skin lesion—such as a new spot, sore, bump, mole change, or an area that won’t heal? (Yes/No)
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any new or changing skin spots, bumps, moles, or sores that won’t heal.” “We don’t have any concerns about his skin beyond that his conjunctiva looks pale.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any nosebleeds recently (even a small amount), or blood coming from your nose?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any nosebleeds, and there hasn’t been any blood coming from my nose.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any rash on your trunk (chest, back, or belly)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any rash on my trunk—no spots on the chest, back, or belly. It’s mainly the pauses in breathing during sleep that my mother is concerned about, and she also mentions my conjunctiva looks pale.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any swollen, twisted, or bulging veins in your legs (varicose veins), especially around the calves or ankles?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any swollen, twisted, or bulging veins in my legs—my mother hasn’t noticed anything like that around my calves or ankles.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever been diagnosed with eczema, or have you had recurring itchy, dry, or inflamed skin patches?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t been diagnosed with eczema, and my mother hasn’t noticed any recurring itchy, dry, or inflamed skin patches.” “The only thing she’s concerned about is that I sometimes stop breathing during sleep and that my conjunctiva looks pale.”
